clock_dir_past: makalipas, "after", the ADDITIVE direction of the native clock: the count
of minutes runs forward from the ordinal-named hour ("limang minuto
makalipas ang ika-anim ng umaga" == 06:05).  en.wikipedia.org, "Date and time notation in the Philippines".
clock_dir_to: bago, "before", the SUBTRACTIVE direction of the native clock: the count
runs back from the UPCOMING ordinal-named hour ("labinlimang minuto bago
ang ika-apat ng hapon" == 15:45).  The same source states that this is how
Filipino tells a time past the half hour -- the additive native frame is
not used there.  en.wiktionary.org, bago (preposition, "before"); en.wikipedia.org, "Date and time notation in the Philippines".
clock_fraction_30: medya, the half in the Spanish-lexified clock, which attaches ADDITIVELY to
the hour already named: "alas otso y medya ng gabi" == 20:30 and "alas
kuwatro y medya ng hapon" == 16:30, both worked examples in the source.
That is the opposite direction from the Continental-Germanic bare half, so
the locale sets bare_half_past rather than bare_half_to.  The source spells
the word med'ya/mediya; the apostrophe form is not shipped because the
tokenizer would shear it.  medya has no Wiktionary Tagalog entry -- the
citation is the worked clock examples alone.  en.wikipedia.org, "Date and time notation in the Philippines".
clock_landmark_720: tanghali, "noon".  tanghaling-tapat is CLDR's wide label for the same
point; only the bare noun is shipped, the attributive -ng form being a
linker inflection rather than a separate surface.  en.wiktionary.org, tanghali;
clock_meridiem_am: umaga, "morning", the day-part that fixes an hour in the AM half
("alas sais ng umaga" == 06:05's hour).  en.wiktionary.org, umaga; en.wikipedia.org, "Date and time notation in the Philippines".
clock_meridiem_night: hatinggabi, "midnight".  Night here is the band that crosses midnight, so
the hour twelve under it is 00:00, not noon: "alas dose ng hatinggabi" ==
00:00.  en.wiktionary.org, hatinggabi; en.wikipedia.org, "Date and time notation in the Philippines".
clock_meridiem_pm: hapon, "afternoon"; gabi, "evening/night"; tanghali, "noon".  All three fix
their hour in the PM half: "alas kuwatro y medya ng hapon" == 16:30, "alas
otso y medya ng gabi" == 20:30, "alas dose ng tanghali" == 12:00.  gabi is a
plain PM marker, not a midnight-crossing band: CLDR fil runs it from 16:00
to 24:00 and gives the small hours to umaga/madaling-araw instead, so it
never has to name a 1am.  en.wiktionary.org, hapon; en.wiktionary.org, gabi; en.wiktionary.org, tanghali;
Unicode CLDR 47, fil; en.wikipedia.org, "Date and time notation in the Philippines".
daypart_afternoon_fil: Band boundaries: Unicode CLDR 47 Day Period Rules, locale fil, transcribed
in chronologia/dayparts.py as the afternoon band (12:00-16:00).
daypart_morning_fil: Band boundaries: Unicode CLDR 47 Day Period Rules, locale fil, transcribed
in chronologia/dayparts.py as the morning band (CLDR morning1 + morning2,
00:00-12:00).  Surface: umaga, "morning".  madaling-araw is NOT shipped:
CLDR fil labels its 06:00-12:00 band with it and its 00:00-06:00 band with
umaga, which inverts the dictionary senses (madaling-araw is glossed as the
period between midnight and sunrise), so which band the word names is
daypart_night_fil: Band boundaries: Unicode CLDR 47 Day Period Rules, locale fil, transcribed
in chronologia/dayparts.py as the night band (18:00-00:00).  Surface: gabi,
"evening/night".  CLDR fil labels BOTH its evening band (16:00-18:00) and
its night band with gabi; the word is bound to night alone, the wider of
the two, and the evening band ships no surface rather than a second reading
marker_and: y, the Spanish-derived "and" that joins an hour to its half in the
Spanish-lexified clock ("alas kuwatro y medya").  It is optional before a
minute count ("alas tres (y) kuwarenta singko").  en.wiktionary.org, y; en.wikipedia.org, "Date and time notation in the Philippines".
marker_ang: ang, the subject case marker, which introduces the target hour of a
subtractive or additive minute count ("bago ang ika-apat").  en.wiktionary.org, ang;
en.wikipedia.org, "Date and time notation in the Philippines".
marker_at: The clock lead-in.  alas and ala are both glossed as the adverb "o'clock":
ala stands before the hour one ("ala una"), alas before every other hour
("alas dose").  Wiktionary's ika- entry names alas as the synonym of the
ordinal-hour construction, which is the other half of this locale's clock.
en.wiktionary.org, alas; en.wiktionary.org, ala; en.wiktionary.org, ika-.
marker_every: tuwing, "every time".  The rival mechanism -- reduplicating the unit noun
(araw-araw, buwan-buwan, taon-taon) -- is not shipped: it is a closed set of
derived adverbs rather than a marker, linggo-linggo has no entry at all, and
nothing sources whether the two are interchangeable.  en.wiktionary.org, tuwing.
marker_future: sa, the oblique marker, glossed for "the time of occurrence: at; on; in;
during", with the worked example "Sa Lunes kami uuwi" ("We're going home on
marker_last: nakaraan, "past"/"last", with its linker form; and noong, the adverb that
"indicates past time", which is what selects the PRECEDING instance of a
named day ("noong Lunes" == the Monday just gone, not the coming one).
marker_mag: mag, the verbal particle the subtractive clock optionally takes before its
target hour: both "bago ang ika-apat" and "bago mag ika-anim" are attested
for the same construction.  en.wikipedia.org, "Date and time notation in the Philippines".
marker_minute_word: minuto, spoken between the count and the direction word in the native
clock ("labinlimang minuto bago ang ika-apat").  en.wikipedia.org, "Date and time notation in the Philippines".
marker_na: na, the linker in its free-standing form.  A Filipino modifier takes the
ligature written onto itself after a vowel ("dalawang araw") but written as
a separate word after a consonant ("anim na buwan", "apat na araw"); the two
are one morpheme, so the counted-unit orders accept either shape.
marker_next: susunod, "next", with its linker form.  en.wiktionary.org, susunod.
marker_ng: ng, the oblique linker.  It stands between a day-ordinal and its month
("ika-24 ng Agosto") and between an hour and its day-part ("alas sais ng
umaga").  en.wiktionary.org, ng; en.wikipedia.org, "Date and time notation in the Philippines".
marker_past: noon, the adverb that "indicates past time", and noong, the same word
carrying the regular -ng linker before what it marks.  en.wiktionary.org, noon.
marker_weekday_counted_ambiguous: linggo names both Sunday and the week, so a count before it ("dalawang
linggo") is ambiguous between a span of weeks and a number of Sundays.  The
count vetoes the weekday reading -- handing back one specific Sunday to a
caller who asked for a duration would be a worse answer than none -- and
the duration reading is not asserted in its place: the week unit this
locale ships is semana, not linggo.  en.wiktionary.org, linggo (noun, "week");
marker_year_word: taon, "year", and taong, its linker form, which introduces a spelled year
in a date ("(taong) dalawang libo't dalawampu't dalawa").  en.wiktionary.org, taon;
en.wikipedia.org, "Date and time notation in the Philippines".

named_day_-2: kamakalawa, "the day before yesterday".  Its mirror, makalawa ("the day
after tomorrow"), is NOT shipped: the same bare word is also the frequency
adverb "twice", the named-day grammar matches it bare, and no source gives
a disambiguator that survives tokenization.  en.wiktionary.org, kamakalawa;

unit_month: buwan, "month" -- and also "moon".  As with araw/sun, the non-temporal sense
